XMage Access - Changelog
========================

What changed in each release, newest first.

Every release is a drop-in replacement: put the new
xmage-access-0.1.0.jar into xmage/mage-client/lib/ over the old one.
Nothing else in this ZIP has to be copied again unless a release says
so. The JAR keeps the name xmage-access-0.1.0.jar in every release -
the launcher scripts look for that name, so it never changes. The
release you have is the one at the top of this file.

The full history, with the reasoning behind every change, is at
github.com/CatalystForChaos/xmage-access.


v0.1.14 - 16 September 2026
---------------------------

Windows instead of shortcuts. Four more places in XMage - the waiting
room, drafts, tournaments and the news page - now have an accessible
window of their own, built like the lobby window: everything is a row
in a list, reached with Tab and the arrow keys, acted on with Enter.
A lot of shortcuts are gone because of that; they are listed under
"Shortcuts removed" below. The keyboard also finds its way back to
the right window on its own now.

New

- Waiting room window. Creating or joining a table opens "XMage
  Accessible Waiting Room" instead of leaving you in XMage's silent
  dialog. Four lists: Table (kind of table, game type, deck type,
  seats taken, state, owner), Seats (one row per seat with player
  name and player type, D reads the whole entry), Actions (Start the
  game or Start the tournament for the table owner, Leave the table
  for everyone) and Chat. Players joining or leaving and the table
  becoming ready are announced. Seats cannot be moved up or down from
  here; XMage's own buttons for that are not offered.

- Draft window. A draft opens "XMage Accessible Draft" with three
  lists: Draft (pack, pick number, time remaining, how many cards are
  in the booster, how many you have picked), Booster and Your Picks.
  Enter in the booster picks the card. A new pack announces itself
  with the first card in it.

- Tournament window. A tournament opens "XMage Accessible
  Tournament" with Tournament (name, type, state, how many players
  and matches), Standings, Matches and Chat, plus a box to type into
  the tournament chat. Enter watches a match that is being played
  right now.

- The news page is a window. XMage's "What's new" dialog draws its
  page in a web view, where a screen reader finds nothing at all - on
  the first launch after a news update the client simply seemed to
  stop responding. It now opens "XMage Access - What's new": the page
  as one row per block, headings ending in "heading" and lines with a
  link ending in "link", a Sections list to jump from heading to
  heading, and an Actions list to open the page in your browser, copy
  it, or close it. Enter on a line with a link opens that link in
  your browser. Escape closes.

- Game actions from the keyboard. Everything XMage hides in the
  right-click menu of the play area is reachable now: Ctrl+Shift+F3
  to F11 mirror XMage's own F3 to F11 skip keys, which are dead while
  you are in the accessible window; Ctrl+Shift+H holds priority; and
  Ctrl+K opens the rest as one filterable list - the skip actions,
  the three mana payment options, the auto-answer resets, rolling
  back 1 to 3 turns, viewing a player's deck or sideboard, asking for
  or granting permission to see hand cards, conceding the game or the
  match, and stopping a spectated game. Conceding and stopping ask
  first.

- Five dialogs that used to say nothing: the join table dialog, the
  add lands dialog, XMage's error dialog, registration, and password
  reset.

- A log file. The agent writes xmage-access.log next to the client
  (the folder XMage runs in, or your home folder if that one cannot
  be written), starting a new one at every launch. Launched through
  XMage's own launcher the client has no console, so this file is the
  only diagnostic there is - send it with a bug report.

Changed

- The agent takes no keys inside XMage's own window any more. Its
  shortcuts answer while one of its own windows is in front; XMage's
  window keeps its keyboard to itself. The exceptions are Ctrl+Q to
  quit and the shortcuts of XMage's own dialogs, which have no
  accessible window of their own.

- An accessible window takes the keyboard when it opens. Before, a
  window that opened behind XMage's frame got neither the focus nor
  any of its shortcuts, and you had to Alt+Tab to it.

- After a match, and whenever one of the agent's windows closes, the
  keyboard goes to the accessible window of whatever XMage now shows
  in front - after a game that is usually the lobby. XMage does not
  return to the lobby by itself, it returns to whichever pane was in
  front before, so the agent walks its panes front to back and takes
  the first one that still has a window.

- Lists no longer re-read the selected row when they refresh. Every
  list is refreshed on a timer, and it used to be emptied and
  refilled, which moved the selection off its row and back again -
  something screen readers announce. Rows are replaced in place now.
  A row that stands for something you can act on - a card, a button,
  a match - and changes under the cursor is read out on purpose; rows
  that are only information - the draft clock, chat, the game log -
  change silently.

- Announcements no longer name shortcuts that were removed. The
  choices they used to name are rows in the Actions list.

Shortcuts removed

All of these only spoke a row that the arrow keys now reach:

- In the lobby: Ctrl+G, Ctrl+J, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+Up, Ctrl+Down and the
  rest of the lobby's thirteen keys. Open games are the Open Games
  list; New Game, New Tournament, Open Deck Editor, Download Images,
  Preferences and Connect / Disconnect are rows in Actions.
- In the join table dialog: everything except Ctrl+D for the deck.
- In a game: the hand cursor (Ctrl+Left, Ctrl+Right, Ctrl+Enter,
  Ctrl+D), the battlefield cursor (Ctrl+Shift+Left, Ctrl+Shift+Right,
  Ctrl+Shift+Up, Ctrl+Shift+Down, Ctrl+Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Shift+D),
  the buttons (Ctrl+1, Ctrl+2, Ctrl+3), undo (Ctrl+Z), targets and
  abilities (Ctrl+T, Ctrl+Shift+1 to Ctrl+Shift+9) and jumping to the
  chat box (Ctrl+M). The zone reads Ctrl+F1 to Ctrl+F11, the game log
  reads, Ctrl+Shift+M, Ctrl+K and the skip keys stay.
- In drafts and tournaments: Ctrl+R, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+M and Ctrl+F1.
  What they read is the first list of each window now.
- In the waiting room: Ctrl+Enter and Ctrl+Shift+I.

Fixed

- Deck editor filters inverted themselves and could take the client
  down. Ctrl+1 for White switched White off and every other colour
  on, because the click the agent sent carried the Ctrl key, which
  XMage reads as "select all the others". With every filter on and no
  set or search term, XMage answers with its whole card database -
  92,030 printings, each built into a card object on the drawing
  thread - and resetting the filters did that eighteen times over.
  A filter now changes one button and runs one pass.

- Ctrl+A in the deck editor did nothing. Swing consults a list's own
  keys before the window's, and a list binds Ctrl+A to "select all",
  so Add Lands never fired. It is bound on the lists themselves now.

- XMage's random packs selector is left alone. It is usable through
  the Java Access Bridge, so the agent no longer speaks or takes keys
  in it.


v0.1.13 - 27 August 2026
------------------------

One deck editor improvement, plus a build safeguard.

- Ctrl+E in the deck editor opens an accessible set list instead of
  asking you to type a set name. Every entry is spoken while you
  browse with Up and Down; PageUp, PageDown, Home and End work too.
  Typing letters narrows the list, Backspace widens it again, Enter
  picks, Escape cancels.
- Picking a set lists all of its cards, 100 per page. Ctrl+T and
  Ctrl+Shift+T still cycle sets one by one.
- The picker resolves the chosen set by name at the moment you pick
  it, so XMage's synthetic "Multiple sets selected" entry can no
  longer shift the list and land you on the wrong set.
- Build: the JAR is compiled against the real Java 8 API when it is
  built on a newer JDK. Before, a call to a Java 9 or later API could
  compile cleanly and then fail at runtime on the Java 8 that XMage
  requires.


v0.1.12 - 16 July 2026
----------------------

In-game chat, and two deck editor features.

- In-game chat, finally reachable. The accessible game window has a
  "Send Game Chat Message" box at the bottom: type and press Enter to
  send to the chat of the running game, the one your opponent sees.
  Before, only the server-wide chat in the lobby could be reached.
- A Chat list in the game window with the last 10 player messages.
  Incoming messages are still announced as they arrive, and
  Ctrl+Shift+M reads the last 5.
- Deck editor: search results are shown 100 per page, with "Next
  page" and "Previous page" entries at the ends of the list. The
  announcement says where you are ("Page 2 of 6. Results 101 to 200
  of 543.") and puts you on the first card of the page. Your page is
  kept while you add and remove cards.
- Deck editor: Ctrl+E browses a whole set.


v0.1.11 - 8 July 2026
---------------------

A full bug sweep.

- Every dialog ever opened used to leak its keyboard hook. Handlers
  whose dialog has closed are swept up now, so keys, timers and chat
  listeners are released instead of piling up for the whole session.
  Dialogs XMage reuses, such as Download Images, are announced again
  the next time they open.
- Choice dialogs own their shortcuts during a game. Confirming a scry
  selection used to play a card from your hand, and Ctrl+1 on a
  concede prompt clicked the game's OK button instead.
- Lobby shortcuts no longer fire underneath a modal dialog.
- Closing the accessible game window resets the state and a fresh
  window opens for the next game; it used to hide for good.
- Switching tabs during a game no longer announces "Game ended." and
  wipes the game window.
- The accessible lobby window comes back after a game instead of
  disappearing the first time the lobby is hidden.
- A momentary failure to read the game id no longer triggers a
  spurious "New game." and a full state reset.
- Draft: a failed display refresh after a pick no longer reports
  "Error picking card" when the pick had already been sent.
- Reconnecting announces the lobby again.
- Windows SAPI speech is fast. One persistent speech worker replaces
  a new PowerShell process per utterance, which had added one to two
  seconds to every announcement and let announcements overlap.
- Hybrid, Phyrexian, tap, snow and energy mana symbols are spoken as
  words instead of raw braces, and revealed-card dialogs speak mana
  costs properly.
- HTML entities are no longer decoded twice, and chat messages are
  split per line again.
- Escape returns the focus to XMage's real window instead of an
  arbitrary one.


v0.1.10 - 20 May 2026
---------------------

An audit pass: leaks, speech and speed.

- Speech never blocks the client. Every engine call runs on a
  background thread, a burst of announcements collapses to the latest
  one, and identical text within 250 milliseconds is dropped.
- Listeners, timers and child processes are released on shutdown.
- Reflection lookups are cached, so the polling that watches the game
  state costs almost nothing.
- A debug log channel, switched on with -Dxmageaccess.log=debug.


v0.1.9 - 25 March 2026
----------------------

- Closing the accessible game window wipes all cached game state, so
  opening it again starts clean. Useful if announcements ever get out
  of step with the game.


v0.1.8 - 25 March 2026
----------------------

- Ctrl+F2 and the other read commands no longer report turn, life
  totals or phase from the previous game of a match. Game data is
  read fresh each time a key fires, not only on the poll cycle.
- The accessible game window reopens for the next game of a match. It
  was disposed when a game ended and never came back.


v0.1.7 - 25 March 2026
----------------------

- Lobby: joining, watching or reading a game that disappeared between
  two refreshes no longer throws an error or acts on the wrong game.
  It says "Game list has changed" instead.


v0.1.6 - 25 March 2026
----------------------

- Nineteen handlers leaked their keyboard hooks. The hooks piled up
  across dialogs and games and fired for components that no longer
  existed; they are removed now when a handler detaches.
- The game window and the deck editor window stop their timers when
  they close, sideboarding no longer stacks up refresh timers when
  cards are moved quickly, and the tournament timer stops on detach.
- The chat listener is removed with the handler that added it.
- A card with no mana cost no longer crashes a list refresh.
- Cancelling speech on Linux no longer leaves zombie processes.


v0.1.5 - 25 March 2026
----------------------

- Ctrl+F2 and the other reads reported the previous game's data.
  XMage replaces its game data object when a new game starts, and the
  agent was holding on to the old one.


v0.1.4 - 20 March 2026
----------------------

- Type-ahead in the lists is suppressed properly. v0.1.3 removed it
  where Swing installs its own handler first, so it kept working; the
  lists now intercept typed keys before any listener sees them.


v0.1.3 - 20 March 2026
----------------------

- Typing a letter in a list no longer moves the selection. Pressing D
  to read a card's detail used to jump to the nearest card starting
  with D at the same time. Arrow keys and shortcuts are unaffected.


v0.1.2 - 16 March 2026
----------------------

- Game state resets between the games of a match, for good. The agent
  follows the game's id, which XMage changes for every game, and
  wipes life totals, turn, phase, stack and hand when it changes. The
  turn-counter guess of v0.1.1 could miss.


v0.1.1 - 9 March 2026
---------------------

- Life totals, turn, phase and stack are reset when a second game
  starts at the same table, instead of producing announcements like
  "Player gained 20 life" from the difference to the first game.


v0.1.0 - 23 February 2026
-------------------------

First public release. A Java agent that adds screen reader support to
the XMage client without changing XMage itself: NVDA, JAWS and
Windows SAPI on Windows, VoiceOver on macOS.

Covered at release: the connect dialog, the lobby with an accessible
window, new game and new tournament, the deck editor, sideboarding,
drafts and the tournament panel, gameplay with prompts, hand,
battlefield, stack, targets, chat and phase announcements, all the
choice dialogs (pick one, pick a number, checkboxes, piles,
distribute), download images, preferences, revealed cards, and Ctrl+Q
to quit.
